title: Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF and Peer Comps
web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF and Peer Comps
question: What does $309.48 already require from an LNG infrastructure company whose cash flow is durable but still cyclical?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay, value is what you get.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett, quoting Ben Graham, 2013 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter [31]

web_blocks.text: Cheniere closed at $309.48 on 12 November 2026. The price was above the rising 50-day average and within a Stage 2 markup, but 2.27 ATR above that average and only 6.43% below its 52-week high. The S&P 500 was in Correction. A sound operating franchise and a constructive chart do not make every entry price attractive; the market has already capitalized a meaningful part of the contracted cash-flow story. [2][12]

Cheniere raised its 2026 Adjusted EBITDA range to $8.75–$9.25 billion and Distributable Cash Flow (DCF) range to $6.05–$6.55 billion after Q3. Those are company-defined forward measures, not GAAP earnings or cash guaranteed to common shareholders. DCF is a useful anchor only alongside growth capital, project debt, derivative timing and noncontrolling interests. [3][20]

web_blocks.title: Why a historical P/E band misleads

web_blocks.caption: Reported earnings changed with the buildout and derivative marks
rows: Several loss years during construction; capital spending exceeded CFO in most early years. [12][24–29]
P/E is not meaningful in negative-EPS years and does not isolate mature liquefaction economics.
$1.428B parent net income in 2022; $9.881B in 2023, including a large derivative fair-value gain. [2][12]
Peak GAAP EPS makes a spot P/E look unusually cheap.
$3.252B and $5.330B parent-attributable net income, respectively; derivative marks remained material. [2][12]
One or two years cannot define normalized earnings for this contract and commodity mix.
$736M parent-attributable net income after $3.6B of unfavorable derivative fair-value variance, while adjusted EBITDA and volumes rose. [3][20]
A single-cycle P/E band would mix accounting marks, physical deliveries and recurring fee economics.
web_blocks.takeaway: We do not present a falsely precise 10-year P/E band. The valuation decision uses a transparent DCF sensitivity and a qualified peer snapshot.

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF: cash yield embedded in the close

web_blocks.text: At $309.48 and 206.9 million Q3 diluted weighted-average shares, the equity-capitalization proxy is about $64.0 billion. Dividing by the $6.30 billion midpoint of 2026 DCF guidance gives 10.16x proxy price-to-DCF, or a 9.84% DCF yield. Under an assumed 10% equity hurdle and a simplified perpetuity, that multiple implies roughly 0.16% perpetual DCF growth. This is not a full DCF: the cash measure is non-GAAP, the share count is a quarterly average, and the hurdle is an analyst assumption. It shows the quote does not require aggressive growth if current cash generation persists; lower normalized DCF, growth spending or parent claims would quickly weaken the result. [3][12][20]

web_blocks.the_number: 10.16x proxy price-to-DCF; 9.84% implied DCF yield at the 12 Nov close
web_blocks.how_calculated: $309.48 × 206.9M diluted weighted-average shares ÷ $6.30B midpoint DCF = 10.16x. At a 10% equity hurdle, implied perpetuity growth is approximately 10% − 1/10.16 = 0.16%.
web_blocks.the_inputs: FY2026 DCF guidance is $6.05B–$6.55B; Q3 diluted weighted-average shares are 206.9M; verified close is $309.48. DCF is company-defined and is not identical to free cash flow available to common owners.
web_blocks.the_range: At a 9% hurdle the simplified growth implication is −0.84%; at 11% it is +1.16%. These are sensitivities, not forecasts.
web_blocks.if_off: If derivative settlements, growth capex, debt service or noncontrolling claims make DCF less distributable than assumed, this proxy overstates equity value. A full-year DCF result below the $6.05B guide floor would break the base case.

web_blocks.caption: Analyst valuation sensitivity—not consensus targets or company guidance
web_blocks.takeaway: At the close, the base value is only 0.82:1 against the $278.52 stop. At the upper end of the $284.10–$297.07 support band, the same base value offers 2.04:1. The arithmetic supports waiting for a pullback.

web_blocks.title: Peer snapshot: same molecule, different business models

web_blocks.text: No clean public pure-play peer set exists. Venture Global is a new U.S. exporter; Sempra combines regulated utilities with LNG projects; Woodside is an upstream producer with a substantial LNG portfolio; Shell is a diversified integrated major. Their ratios cannot erase differences in project stage, ownership, leverage or non-LNG earnings. Venture Global’s Q3 release confirms that new supply is operational competition, reporting 124 cargoes and $2.6 billion of quarterly Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA. [17][30]

web_blocks.caption: LNG and listed LNG / infrastructure comparators; closing prices and stages aligned to 12 Nov 2026, vendor fundamentals captured intraday 13 Nov at 10:46 ET
web_blocks.takeaway: Ledger-aligned stages were LNG Stage 2, VG Stage 3, SRE Stage 4, WDS Stage 1 and SHEL Stage 3. P/E, ROE, growth, operating margin and market-cap fields remain from the next-morning vendor snapshot and are directional context only; they are not same-session valuation spreads. [12][32]

web_blocks.text: The base sensitivity is $25.46 above the close while the stop is $30.96 below it, a 0.82:1 reward-to-risk ratio. The proposed pullback zone uses the verified 50- and 20-day averages, $284.10–$297.07; from its upper edge, the base sensitivity offers 2.04:1 against the $278.52 stop. Given the conditional business quality, the hurdle is not met at the close but is met at support, subject to the fundamental and market checks in Chapter 9. [3][12][20]

book_paragraphs: Let us begin with the price you would pay. LNG closed at $309.48 on 12 November. It was above the rising 50-day average and near its annual high, but the broader market was in Correction and the shares had already traveled more than two ATRs above that average. The relevant question is not whether Cheniere owns valuable assets. It is whether the price leaves enough room for the parts of the business neither contracts nor engineering can control: global supply, derivative timing, capital cost and project execution. [2][12]

You and I should be cautious with a historical P/E band. During the construction years Cheniere recorded losses. In 2023, parent-attributable earnings rose to $9.881 billion with a large derivative fair-value gain. In 2026, nine-month net income fell to $736 million after a $3.6 billion unfavorable derivative variance even as operating volume and adjusted EBITDA increased. Physical cargoes, hedge marks and cash collection do not move on the same calendar. A ten-year median P/E would look precise while mixing fundamentally different operating states. [2][3][12]

The reverse-DCF check is intentionally small. Q3 diluted weighted-average shares of 206.9 million multiplied by the verified close imply roughly $64.0 billion of equity capitalization. Against the $6.30 billion midpoint of company DCF guidance, that is 10.16 times DCF, or a 9.84% yield proxy. DCF is not GAAP free cash flow available to owners; it is company-defined and must be read beside maintenance, growth spending, debt service, derivative settlements and outside ownership. [3][20]

At an assumed 10% equity hurdle, a simplified perpetuity at 10.16 times cash flow implies almost no perpetual DCF growth. That does not make the shares obviously cheap. It means the current quote can be supported if today’s cash guide is durable and the capital structure does not absorb more of it than the proxy assumes. If DCF falls below guidance, project capital rises, or the margin of new contracts shrinks, the apparent yield can be a mirage. [3][12]

The bear case assigns DCF 20% below midpoint and an 8x multiple for $194.88 per share. The base case uses the midpoint at 11x for $334.94. The bull case assumes 15% DCF growth and a 12x multiple for $420.20. These are our scenarios, not management targets. The base case offers modest upside at the close and much better geometry after a pullback to support. [3][20]

Comparisons help only when their limits are visible. Venture Global competes directly in U.S. liquefaction; Sempra also earns utility returns; Woodside produces upstream hydrocarbons; Shell combines trading, production and downstream businesses. The 13 November morning snapshot includes next-session vendor fundamentals, even though closes and technical stages were aligned to the 12 November ledger. Do not treat its ratios as a clean relative-value ranking or use them as order levels. [12][17][30][32]

The action follows from that asymmetry. The price is observable; the $334.94 base value is an analyst scenario; the $278.52 stop is a technical invalidation level. At the close, the base reward is less than the planned downside. At the top of the support band, the same case clears the 1.5:1 minimum. Waiting does not reject the operating franchise; it refuses to pay a price that has not yet earned the new-capital hurdle. [12]

book_subsections.title: What the valuation can and cannot say
paragraphs: The midpoint DCF is a useful current reference, not a ten-year forecast. We do not splice commodity spot prices or an unsupported discount rate into a long-range model and present the result as intrinsic value. Instead, we state the current guide, the multiple assigned to each scenario, the assumed hurdle and the conditions that invalidate the comparison.

If the company delivers the guide, ramps CCL Stage 3 reliably and funds each future phase on sound commercial terms, the base-to-bull range becomes more plausible. If contract spreads compress, derivative settlements consume cash or construction capital overruns, the bear case gains weight. The verdict depends on those signposts as much as on the price multiple.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A valuation model earns trust by showing what it cannot know. Here the useful signal is not a magic fair value; it is the gap between a modest at-close reward and a stronger support-zone setup. Keep the operating thesis and the entry decision separate.
